report.answer_text:
President Donald Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1, Public Law 119-21) on July 4, 2025. The law made many of the 2017 tax cuts permanent, reduced projected federal spending on Medicaid and food assistance, and increased funding for immigration enforcement and defense. (govinfo.gov)
| Area | Main provisions |
|---|---|
| Individual taxes | Made the 2017 individual income-tax rates and larger standard deduction permanent. Raised the maximum child tax credit to $2,200 per qualifying child for 2025 and temporarily raised the state and local tax (SALT) deduction cap to $40,000 for most filers in 2025, with a return to $10,000 in 2030. Created temporary deductions for qualifying tips, overtime premiums, certain auto-loan interest, and eligible seniors for 2025–2028. (everycrsreport.com) |
| Business taxes and children’s accounts | Restored immediate deductions for qualifying equipment and domestic research expenses. Created tax-advantaged “Trump Accounts” for children, with a $1,000 federal contribution for eligible U.S. citizen children born from 2025 through 2028. (everycrsreport.com) |
| Medicaid and health coverage | Added work or other qualifying-activity requirements for many adults covered through Medicaid expansion, tightened eligibility checks, and limited some ways states finance Medicaid. It also tightened eligibility for certain Affordable Care Act marketplace subsidies and created a $50 billion rural health program. (congress.gov) |
| Food assistance (SNAP) | Expanded work requirements to more adults, narrowed noncitizen eligibility, and shifted some program costs to states, including a share of benefit costs for states with higher payment-error rates. (everycrsreport.com) |
| Immigration and defense | Funded border barriers, immigration enforcement, and expanded detention capacity, including $45 billion for immigration detention. The defense title provided about $156 billion for priorities including shipbuilding, missile defense, and munitions. (govinfo.gov) |
| Energy and student loans | Ended federal electric-vehicle tax credits early, accelerated the phaseout of several other clean-energy incentives, and expanded federal oil and gas leasing. It also capped federal borrowing for graduate students and parents, ended new Grad PLUS loans with transition exceptions, and restructured repayment options. (irs.gov) |
The law also raised the federal debt ceiling by $5 trillion. The Congressional Budget Office estimated that, relative to its January 2025 baseline, the law would increase federal deficits by $3.4 trillion over fiscal years 2025–2034, before additional interest costs: projected revenue fell by more than projected spending did. (govinfo.gov)

quotes.text: The limitation in tax year 2025 is set to $40,000 ($20,000 for married individuals filing separately); in each subsequent year through tax year 2029, the limitation increases by 1% from its value the previous year.

This chapter also provides for a state and local tax (SALT) deduction cap of $40,000 for most taxpayers in tax year 2025, provides for annual increases for tax years 2026 through 2029, and permanently resets the limit at $10,000 for most taxpayers beginning in tax year 2030.

quotes.text: This provision provides for 100% bonus depreciation for property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025.
This provision restores the domestic research expensing and full basis adjustment rule.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state that the provision provides 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying property (equipment-like assets) placed in service after January 19, 2025, and that it restores domestic research expensing, which together back the claim's restoration of immediate deductions for equipment and domestic research.
pages.page_reason: The page states that the law provides 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025, and restores immediate expensing for domestic research expenditures.

quotes.text: This provision also creates a new one-time refundable tax credit of $1,000 for each qualifying child, which will be contributed to the child's Trump account.
To be eligible for the one-time tax credit, the child must be born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, and be a U.S. citizen.
This provision creates a new type of tax-deferred individual retirement account (IRA) for young people, called a Trump account.

quotes.text: Section 71119 requires certain specified nonpregnant, nondisabled, childless adults, ages 19 through 64, who are eligible for (or are enrolled under) the ACA Medicaid expansion pathway
to complete a minimum of 80 hours of qualifying community engagement activities for one month
